subject: Next steps — Tool/function calling & deterministic output for FinLytics
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finlytics.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + proposed next steps (tool calls, deterministic schema)

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to surface the concrete next steps: 

Summary of your pain points and goals
- You run a periodic financial-report extraction pipeline that ingests earnings calls, investor decks, and SEC filings. Output must be strictly structured for downstream rules engines and compliance auditing.
- Current LLM outputs are too free-form (NER-like summaries, inconsistent fields), which breaks downstream parsing and manual QA takes ~2 FTEs/week.
- Latency target for per-document enrichment is ~500ms median (burst to 1s acceptable).
- Data residency: production data must stay in their AWS account; PII must never leave FinLytics control.

Current stack (as stated)
- EKS-hosted microservices, some SageMaker endpoints for in-house models, S3 for upstream artifacts, Kafka for events.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- Deterministic JSON output that validates against a canonical schema with >95% pass rate on your sample set.
- Per-request median latency <500ms for single-document calls at expected sizing (100 req/min baseline).
- Reproducible fallback behavior: when schema validation fails, we surface a structured error object (not free text) and route to human-in-the-loop queue.

Redwood approach we discussed
- Use function-calling + schema enforcement for a strict JSON handshake. Redwood will enforce schema at the serving layer and return a validation status field for every response.
- Agent/workflow pattern: primary LLM step -> schema validation -> canonicalizer -> if still invalid, produce structured error with suggested corrections and route to a retry/workflow that runs a deterministic post-processor.
- KV/prefix caching for repeated doc structural patterns (reduces tokens/cost for recurring forms).
- Private deployment/Dedicated capacity options for hosting inside your VPC so data never leaves your AWS account.

Open questions (we captured these on call)
- Are there existing canonical vocabularies or enums we should seed into the schema?
- Can you share a representative sample of 50 documents so we can run internal validation?
- Expected daily volume and peak concurrency (you estimated ~8k docs/day with peaks at 150 req/min).

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline)
- Samir / Priya: share 50-sample set + list of mandatory fields and enums by Fri, Jun 12. (Samir)
- Redwood (Aditya): draft an initial JSON schema and example validator + short proposal for Dedicated trial by Mon, Jun 15. (Aditya)
- Schedule technical deep-dive: 60m session for agent/workflow walk-through and security architecture (Ben + Marissa to attend). Target Wed, Jun 17 — Ben to pick times. (Ben)

Attachments: I’m attaching a one-page proposal and a sample schema skeleton that is intentionally sparse — would rather iterate on your samples.

If that looks right I’ll start the schema draft and book the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A few clarifications: 

- We do have required enums for sectors and instrument types (I’ll export those).
- Sample set: I can share 60 docs (sanitized) by EOD Friday — they include both earnings transcripts and structured SEC tables.
- On latency: 500ms is a target for the enrichment step only (we accept pre/post-processing outside that window).

Also: security note — we require a copy of the audit trail for schema validation events (time, model id, validation result) retained for 180 days. Can Redwood surface that in logs or a dedicated API?

I’ll attach a quick sample of a problematic output (shows how fields get reordered and nested inconsistently).

—Samir
